cells.tense: You're in it now — the pull toward what connects is moving, and you're moving with it.
cells.ask: Tell one person why a thing matters to you, not just that it does. Then stop and let them answer.
cells.core:
You're in it right now. There's a pull in you toward what connects, and you're not standing outside examining it. You're teaching, sharing, making meaning with whoever is in the room — and it's working because you're actually present to it instead of managing it.

Here's what that looks like when it's clean: you say why something matters and the why lands, people pick it up and carry it further than you did. The pull stays a pull, not a performance. You hold it lightly — you can stay generous with complicated people, which is the harder part. So let it keep moving: give one reason out loud instead of only feeling it, and the connection gets more room to grow.

cells.verb: moving people toward shared meaning by feeling your way there
cells.place: the pull you orient by, recognised rather than given

cells.tense: You're already living in the conversation where they finally get it, and it hasn't happened yet.
cells.ask: Say the one thing once and sit with the silence after. Don't add a second reason.
cells.core:
You're pushing toward a scene where the other person finally understands. Not the conversation happening now — the one where it's landed, where the shared meaning has arrived and both of you are on the same page. So you keep adding reasons, keep reaching for one more example, because you can feel the conversation that works and you want it here now.

The problem is the reach. Bracing for the moment it lands keeps you out of the room you're actually in. You're in the proof, not the person. The intensity that makes connection happen can also talk over it. So give the thing once, in your own words, and leave it — let the quiet afterward do some of the work.

cells.tense: You were in the middle of it a while back, and you're still standing at that door.
cells.ask: Write down one idea you care about in plain rough words, and leave it where you'll see it this week.
cells.core:
You've got the warmth that moves people and you're not spending it. The offering has gotten careful — you watch connection happen around you more than you're inside it, and the pull you used to answer feels farther off than it did.

So don't push more feeling into the place where it's short. Give your mind something sharp to hold instead: say the idea you care about in plain words, without dressing it up, without checking whether it's good. That kind of clarity travels. Understanding a thing well enough to see its shape clearly gives the warmth somewhere to go, and the pull starts moving again on its own rather than being forced.

cells.tense: You're steering people toward something already, though you'd call it just how you talk.
cells.ask: Catch one thing you said that changed the room, and tell yourself plainly: that was chosen.
cells.core:
You're already shaping what the people around you care about. Not loudly — in what you emphasise, what you laugh at, what you let pass without comment. The pull toward what connects runs through you and out into the room, and it's doing real work. Ask about it and you'd say you were just being yourself, or just talking.

That's the gap. The influence is real and it's yours, and the ownership hasn't caught up. So notice one moment this week where what you said turned a conversation a certain way. Don't do anything about it yet — just see it as a choice you made. Naming it once is how it becomes something you can pick up or set down, instead of a current you're riding without knowing.

attempts.check: Unsupported claim: that the person's 'star' is a specific direction already recognised, where the record only says Inspiration is orientation toward what is genuinely desired. A reader could reasonably say 'I don't actually know which one is mine,' so the ask in each cell must work as a small act of contact rather than a verdict on what they want. The ask survives being wrong because it asks for one observable move — naming a person, staying in a room, writing before it's ready — and teaches something either way. The sentence that serves me rather than them is any version of 'you already know,' which would flatter the read at their expense; it is cut.
